description: Minimal zero-allocation HTTP/1.x server for .NET 8+. Native AOT compatible. Built on raw sockets with a sliding receive window and pooled buffers for an allocation-free steady-state fast path.
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes (with migration):
   1 - HttpMethod is renamed to RequestMethod; the old name collided with System.Net.Http.HttpMethod, which ImplicitUsings imports into every console project. Replace HttpMethod with RequestMethod and drop any "using HttpMethod = Anka.HttpMethod;" alias.
   2 - MultipartParser and MultipartPart moved from Anka.Internal to the Anka namespace. Remove "using Anka.Internal;".
   3 - WriteAsync and StartChunkedResponseAsync throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for status codes below 200 or above 999 (1xx codes cannot be a final response).
   4 - The CancellationToken passed to the handler is now cancelled when the shutdown timeout expires, not as soon as shutdown starts.
   5 - Server no longer writes "Listening on ..." to standard output. Subscribe to Server.ListeningStarted if you relied on it.
   New:
   6 - Graceful shutdown: cancelling the StartAsync token stops accepting, closes idle connections, lets requests already in the handler finish with Connection: close, and aborts the rest after ServerOptions.ShutdownTimeout (default 10 s; TimeSpan.Zero keeps the old immediate abort). StartAsync returns once every connection has ended.
   7 - IPv6 listening: host "::1" for IPv6 loopback, "::" for all interfaces (dual-stack, also accepts IPv4). ListeningStarted reports the bound endpoint.
   8 - HttpRequest.TryGetRange(length, out start, out end) resolves a single-range Range header (bytes=a-b, a-, -n) for GET requests; pass the result to WritePartialAsync.
   9 - MultipartParser.TryGetBoundary(contentType, out boundary) reads the boundary from a multipart/form-data Content-Type.
   10 - Standard reason phrases for every RFC 9110 status code plus common extensions (e.g. 422 Unprocessable Content, 502 Bad Gateway); unknown codes are sent with an empty reason phrase instead of "Unknown".
   Documentation: README rewritten as a getting-started guide with verified recipes (routing, query strings, JSON source generation, CORS, streaming, Range, ETag, uploads, Docker, shutdown) and an accurate API reference.
